ctx.x: Yeah. Well, a lot in New York City and then around New York City. We went from coast to coast at least four times, see. We went on tours with Louis Armstrong's

band, and that's when he acquired the Louis Russell Orchestra. That's right after W.C. Handy went with Louis Armstrong's band, and the Louis Russell Orchestra, went out to Los Angeles, and back down to New Orleans. That was during the Mardi Gras and so forth, and he was at great fame then. He was practically the most famous jazz musician we had during those years. He was always a great recording star, you see, Louis Satchmo Armstrong, and we got to be like regular families, you see. But as I say, Chuck and…
I'm curious to know what it was like with Louis Armstrong, what sort of fellow he was, what kind of stuff you did with him.
